title: Affine descent of a perfect complex along a filtered colimit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and let $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ be a directed system of commutative rings with colimit $A=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}A_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] (the affine form of a perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-complex]). Then there are an index $i$ and a bounded complex $P_i^\bullet$ of finite projective $A_i$-modules with an isomorphism $P_i^\bullet\otimes_{A_i}A\cong P^\bullet$ of complexes.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.18, Tag 0BC7, label more-algebra-lemma-colimit-perfect (the case A = colim A_i)

proof.text: Choose integers $a\le b$ outside which $P^\bullet$ is zero, and write its finitely many nonzero terms as finite projective modules $P^r$ with differentials $d^r:P^r\to P^{r+1}$. The finite list of terms and maps is the affine data of the given bounded complex.

source.place: Lemma 15.76.18 (Tag 0BC7), proof, reduction to a bounded complex and its finitely many module and differential data

proof.text: Each $P^r$ is finite projective, hence finitely presented (Algebra, Lemma 00NX; Mathlib `Module.finitePresentation_of_projective`). By [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] (modules) there are $i$ and finitely presented $A_i$-modules $M^r$ with isomorphisms $M^r\otimes_{A_i}A\cong P^r$; directedness gives one $i$ for the finitely many $r$. Since $P^r$ is finite projective, a surjection $A^{n}\to P^r$ splits [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], giving $\iota:P^r\to A^n$, $\sigma:A^n\to P^r$ with $\sigma\iota=\mathrm{id}$; here $A^n=A_i^n\otimes_{A_i}A$. By [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] (maps) $\iota,\sigma$ are base changes of maps $\iota_j,\sigma_j$ between $M^r\otimes_{A_i}A_j$ and $A_j^n$ at some $j\ge i$, and by its third clause (equality) $\sigma_j\iota_j=\mathrm{id}$ after a later stage, since both sides become $\mathrm{id}_{P^r}$ over $A$. Then $P_j^r:=M^r\otimes_{A_i}A_j$ is a direct summand of $A_j^n$, hence finite projective, with $P_j^r\otimes_{A_j}A\cong P^r$. One common stage $j$ serves all $r$ (directedness); rename it $i$.

source.place: Lemma 15.76.18 (Tag 0BC7), proof: finitely presented modules form the colimit category (Algebra 05N7/0G8P) and finite projectives are summands of finite free modules (Algebra 00NX)

proof.text: With the term models $P_i^r$ of Step 2 fixed, apply [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] (maps) to each of the finitely many differentials $d^r:P^r\to P^{r+1}$ and pass to one common later index $j$ (directedness): this gives $A_j$-linear maps $d_j^r:P_i^r\otimes_{A_i}A_j\to P_i^{r+1}\otimes_{A_i}A_j$ whose base changes to $A$ are the $d^r$. The composite $d_j^{r+1}d_j^r$ and the zero map both base change to $d^{r+1}d^r=0$, so by the third clause (equality) of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] they agree after a later stage; one stage serves the finitely many $r$. Rename it $i$.

source.place: Lemma 15.76.18 (Tag 0BC7), proof, descent of the differential matrices and the finitely many relations $d^{r+1}d^r=0$

proof.text: The resulting bounded complex $P_i^\bullet$ has finite projective terms and squares to zero. The chosen termwise base-change isomorphisms carry its differentials to those of $P^\bullet$, hence assemble to an isomorphism of complexes $P_i^\bullet\otimes_{A_i}A\cong P^\bullet$.

source.place: Lemma 15.76.18 (Tag 0BC7), conclusion of the affine complex descent argument
